title: Lower bound by the clock parameter
statement: For a profile $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, real numbers $a,b,t,c$, and vectors $u,v\in\mathbb R^m$, one has $\sqrt c\le L(t,c)$, where the real square root is zero for negative arguments.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a real-valued function on the reals
replaced: For a profile $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $a,b,t,c\in\mathbb R$, and $u,v\in\mathbb R^m$, define $L(t,c)=\frac12\bigl(\sqrt{P(a+tb)^2+c+\|u+tv\|_2^2}+\sqrt{P(a-tb)^2+c+\|u-tv\|_2^2}\bigr)$. For every real $t,c$, $\sqrt c\le L(t,c)$, with the real square root taken to be zero on negative arguments.
